reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, RSchedule and recurConfigToRSchedule rather than writing new date machinery; the new handler reuses the getUpcomingDates pattern.

duplication.why: The 'if skipWeekend then getDateWithSkippedWeekend(..., frequency, holidays)' gate is written three times (getOccurrenceDay in schedule-template, applyWeekendSkip in app.ts, inline in getNextDate), the occurrence-take margin formula is repeated in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange copies getUpcomingDates' skeleton.

placement.why: Weekend/holiday rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in server/schedules/app.ts as the tree does; only the per-module gate wrappers are scattered.

scope.why: Changes stay within schedules, the budget template consumer and the type, plus the needed rule-utils data passthrough.

maintainability.why: The core rule is in one function, but the skipWeekend gate and look-ahead margins are copied with different magic numbers across call sites, so future rule changes need edits in several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All consumers still go through getDateWithSkippedWeekend; none bypasses it.

disguised_duplication.where: getOccurrenceDay (budget/schedule-template.ts) and applyWeekendSkip (server/schedules/app.ts) are the same skipWeekend gate under different names and signatures, also inlined in getNextDate (shared/schedules.ts).

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters and a 'frequency === daily -> null' branch; callers each wrap it in their own skipWeekend gate rather than bypassing it.
